title: Why people-pleasing or conflict-avoidance patterns develop
content: Patterns like these are usually learned, often early, from environments where speaking up felt risky, wasn't modeled, or wasn't safe. It made sense as a strategy at the time. The pattern can outlast its usefulness though, showing up even in situations where speaking up now would actually be safe and effective.
